L1.note: Not blocked yet. Home Assistant docs say Reolink cameras keep working with internet blocked (documented, not yet tested on this unit)

L2.note: Reolink: without internet, local app access, live view, playback and SD recording work; app and Client can add a device by IP

L3.note: Reolink advises internet for the phone and camera at first Wi-Fi setup; whether an account is required is not documented

L4.note: Reolink documents a UID/P2P off switch for powered cameras in the desktop Client (Network > Advanced), not the app; not confirmed present on the E1 Pro, egress stop untested

L5.note: DNS from DHCP only (tested: ONVIF GetDNS and resolver log). NTP is pool.ntp.org; whether it accepts the router as NTP server is untested (one report says Reolink rejects IPs as NTP server, other model)

L6.note: RTSP 554 (Digest, realm 'BC Streaming Media') and ONVIF 8000 on; HTTP/HTTPS closed on this unit

E1.note: Relay payload (1.6 MB): no H.264/HEVC NAL headers after start codes (101 start codes, mostly followed by 0x00 = framing), no Baichuan media headers, entropy 7.79. Assumed encrypted; not decoded

E2.note: No printable identifiers in any egress payload. BcUdp obfuscation not analysed: if it uses a fixed public key, the UID would be recoverable

E3.note: Only p2p.reolink.com and pool.ntp.org, both via the LAN resolver; relay IP handed out by the P2P server

E4.note: Oracle Cloud only (US registration, Sweden relay)

E5.note: Idle: one UDP keep-alive to the relay, ~75 bytes/s

E6.note: RTSP Digest, ONVIF, Baichuan 9000 (login required), P2P 2000/udp; no telnet, HTTP closed

E7.note: No CVE or Talos report found for the E1 Pro/E1 series (search 2026-11-03). Talos 2021-22 CVEs are for the RLC-410W and were patched; not carried over

E8.note: Reolink runs a firmware download center; not checked for this hardware ID

other_observations: First setup needs internet per Reolink; disabling P2P is only in the desktop Client
